geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bent bar with a section-aware massing operator so the building can carry a clearer program section and roof logic.
A folded section can strengthen the silhouette without turning the building into arbitrary tiers.
Keep the dominant section logic aligned with the long direction of the compact site mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Turn the primary mass from a sealed block into a more legible access-facing carved form that can support a public threshold.
Align the void/opening to the programmed access side so the ground response is read at the verified frontage.
Create a substantial but bounded court/undercut rather than a decorative nibble.

rationale: The candidate is coherent as one mass in all four views and does not visibly self-collide, so it passes basic structural legibility. However, it reads primarily as a compact sealed block with a mild top cut rather than as neighborhood living with an active public threshold. The blue access edge is not answered by a clear court, notch, undercut, or entry seam; the ground plane remains mostly closed. The bent/prismatic language has some precedent resonance, but the section does not establish a convincing public void or terrace logic, and the massing does not strongly signal mixed-use neighborhood occupation beyond generic block form. Because the program contract explicitly requires an active edge and usable public space response, the hard program fit fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this low compact neighborhood-living candidate; the candidate lacks the strong vertical hierarchy and urban podium-tower relation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/prismatic massing can still read as a single dominant object when the profile remains continuous and the upper setback is controlled.
